subject: chemistry
title: Energetics & Thermochemistry Adventure 3: Born-Haber, entropy and ΔG
welcome_lead: Today you'll build a Born-Haber cycle and predict spontaneity with ΔG.
meta_desc: Chemistry HL — Born-Haber cycle, lattice energy, entropy ΔS, Gibbs free energy ΔG.
final_note: You learned Born-Haber cycles find lattice enthalpy, ΔS° measures disorder, and ΔG = ΔH − TΔS predicts spontaneity.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Construct a Hess cycle for ionic formation of NaCl:

Na(s) + ½Cl₂(g) → NaCl(s), ΔH_f = -411 kJ/mol.

Steps: atomisation of Na (+108), ionisation of Na (+496), atomisation of Cl (+121), e⁻ affinity of Cl (-349), lattice formation Na⁺(g) + Cl⁻(g) → NaCl(s) (= -ΔH_lat).

Sum equals ΔH_f. Solve for lattice energy ≈ -787 kJ/mol.

Entropy ΔS = disorder. Increases:
- solid → liquid → gas.
- pure → mixture (dissolution).
- more particles produced.

For aA → bB: ΔS° = Σ S°(products) − Σ S°(reactants).

Burning hydrocarbon C₈H₁₈ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O: many gas molecules either side; modest ΔS.

ΔG = ΔH − TΔS

- ΔG < 0: spontaneous.
- ΔG = 0: equilibrium.
- ΔG > 0: not spontaneous.

Examples:
- ΔH < 0, ΔS > 0: always spontaneous.
- ΔH > 0, ΔS < 0: never spontaneous.
- ΔH < 0, ΔS < 0: spontaneous at low T.
- ΔH > 0, ΔS > 0: spontaneous at high T (e.g. melting ice above 0°C).

mcqs.q: Ice melting at 25°C: ΔH > 0, ΔS > 0. At room temperature:
What state are the ions in when defining lattice enthalpy of formation?
options: The ions are in aqueous solution before forming the lattice.
All endothermic reactions are spontaneous at room temperature.
Gaseous ions — lattice enthalpy is the energy change when one mole of solid ionic compound forms from its constituent ions in the GAS phase.
The ions start as solid elements before being assembled into the lattice.

mcqs.q: Why can an endothermic reaction still be spontaneous?
options: If the entropy increase (TΔS) is large enough to outweigh the positive ΔH, ΔG can still be negative.
The entropy of the surroundings must stay constant for the process to be spontaneous.
All endothermic reactions are spontaneous at room temperature.
Endothermic reactions are never spontaneous because they require energy input.

mcqs.q: For a process to be spontaneous, what must happen to the total entropy of the universe?
options: All endothermic reactions are spontaneous at room temperature.
The entropy of the system must increase for the process to be spontaneous.
It must increase (ΔS_total > 0) — the system's entropy alone can decrease as long as the surroundings' entropy increases more.
The entropy of the surroundings must stay constant for the process to be spontaneous.
